skill.name: deeptools
skill.description: NGS analysis toolkit. BAM to bigWig conversion, QC (correlation, PCA, fingerprints), heatmaps/profiles (TSS, peaks), for ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, ATAC-seq visualization.
skill.summary: Plan, validate, and document deepTools workflows for ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and ATAC-seq data.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Four generated Bash-template findings are confirmed because CLI values are embedded without shell escaping, enabling command injection when a workflow runs. The other 94 detections are documentation syntax, unrelated genomics text, or expected local output writes.

remediation.issue: Generated Bash workflows embed user-supplied paths without shell-safe encoding.
remediation.suggestion: Encode every inserted value with shlex.quote, quote all Bash variable expansions, and reject control characters. Prefer direct subprocess calls with argument arrays.

content.value_statement: NGS analysis requires many coordinated commands, parameters, and quality checks. This skill supplies validated guidance, workflow templates, and references for common deepTools analyses.
actual_capabilities: Validates BAM, bigWig, and BED file readability before analysis.
Checks BAM index presence and basic BED coordinate structure.
Generates Bash templates for four ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and ATAC-seq workflows.
Guides selection among RPGC, CPM, RPKM, BPM, and raw-count normalization.
Provides commands for correlation, PCA, fingerprints, heatmaps, profiles, and enrichment plots.
Supplies effective genome sizes and deepTools parameter references.
limitations: deepTools, samtools, Python, and required system resources must be installed separately.
File validation is basic and does not prove BAM, bigWig, or BED biological correctness.
Generated scripts require inspection because supplied paths are inserted into Bash templates.
Workflow defaults require adjustment for library design, genome assembly, and experimental goals.

use_cases.title: Prepare ChIP-seq Quality Control
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable QC workflow covering correlation, PCA, coverage, fragment size, and enrichment.

use_cases.title: Create Strand-Specific Coverage
use_cases.description: Plan forward and reverse RNA-seq coverage tracks with suitable normalization and splice-aware settings.

use_cases.title: Visualize ATAC-seq Signal
use_cases.description: Apply Tn5 correction, generate normalized coverage, and summarize signal around accessible regions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate NGS Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate these NGS files before analysis: [paths]. Explain each failed check and the next corrective action.

prompt_templates.title: Convert BAM to bigWig
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a BAM-to-bigWig conversion for [experiment] in [organism]. Recommend normalization, genome size, filtering, bin size, and processor settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a QC Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a deepTools QC workflow for these samples: [sample list]. Include correlation, PCA, coverage, fingerprints, expected outputs, and interpretation criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Signals Across Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced comparison for [groups] around [genomic features]. Choose normalization, matrix mode, clustering, plots, controls, and reproducibility checks.

output_examples.input: Validate two BAM files and one BED file before ChIP-seq analysis.
output: Both BAM files are readable and have index files.
The BED file has at least three columns with valid coordinate order.
The inputs are ready for initial quality control.

output_examples.input: Recommend normalization for human ChIP-seq coverage tracks.
output_examples.output: Use RPGC for genome-normalized coverage with the matching human assembly size. Apply the same filtering and bin settings across every sample.

output_examples.input: Plan an ATAC-seq heatmap around peak centers.
output_examples.output: Shift alignments for Tn5 offset, create normalized bigWig coverage, compute a centered matrix around peaks, then plot clustered heatmaps and profiles.

best_practices: Validate files and genome assemblies before generating any workflow.
Run quality control before comparison, clustering, or publication plots.
Inspect generated scripts and use trusted, shell-safe file paths.
anti_patterns: Do not compare samples with inconsistent normalization or filtering settings.
Do not extend RNA-seq reads across splice junctions.
Do not execute generated scripts before reviewing paths, outputs, and resource settings.

faq.question: Does this skill install deepTools?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but deepTools and supporting command-line tools must be installed in the execution environment.

faq.question: Which sequencing assays are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq, and related assays using BAM, bigWig, bedGraph, and BED files.

faq.question: Can it validate my input files?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper checks readability, BAM indexes, bigWig size, and basic BED coordinates, but it does not verify biological validity.

faq.question: Which normalization method should I choose?
faq.answer: The choice depends on assay and comparison goals. The skill explains RPGC, CPM, RPKM, BPM, and read-count approaches.

faq.question: Does it run a complete analysis automatically?
faq.answer: It generates workflow templates and command guidance. You must review parameters, install dependencies, and execute approved commands in your environment.

faq.question: Are generated workflows safe to execute unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Review every generated script, especially file paths and output directories, because the current generator does not shell-escape supplied values.
